incident: The edge service latency and error rate spiked; customers report timeouts.
title: Edge Service CPU Starvation and Timeouts Caused by WAF Rules Configuration Change

root_cause.statement: A newly introduced regular expression in the edge-waf-rules ConfigMap caused heavy CPU consumption and request blocking, leading to severe CPU starvation, high latency, and probe timeouts on the edge pods.

confidence.label: high
confidence.explanation: High: the leading cause is supported by multiple independent sources and nothing strongly contradicts it.

causal_chain.step: ConfigMap edge-waf-rules was modified at 2026-10-13T13:02:46+00:00 with new WAF rule patterns.
Edge pods experienced high CPU throttling and starvation immediately following the configuration change.
CPU exhaustion on edge pods led to failing liveness and readiness probes, causing container restarts and degraded service availability.
Edge services failed to communicate with upstream dependencies due to timeouts, resulting in a spike in 5xx error rates and customer-facing timeouts.

facts.statement: The edge deployment has only 2 out of 3 replicas ready.
The HPA for edge is currently at its maximum replica limit of 3.

facts.quote: Liveness probe failed: Get "http://10.244.1.97:8080/healthz": context deadline exceeded
facts.statement: Edge pods are experiencing liveness probe timeouts on /healthz.
The CPU utilization for the edge HPA target is extremely high at 447%.
Edge pods are experiencing connection timeouts when calling the checkout service.
Dependency failures for checkout (connect_error) surged starting at 12:54:55Z.
CPU throttling on edge pods jumped significantly starting at 13:03:25Z after the WAF rules configmap update.
Edge pod container restarts began increasing at 13:04:10Z.
Checkout workload metrics show an increase in error ratio 5xx starting at 2026-10-13T12:46:15Z.
Edge pod previous instance logs show numerous ConnectTimeout errors when calling checkout.
Checkout dependency failures towards inventory (connect_error) increased starting at 2026-10-13T12:46:15Z.

hypotheses.statement: The newly added regex in edge-waf-rules causes heavy CPU consumption or request blocking, leading to CPU starvation, high latency, and probe timeouts on edge pods.
hypotheses.mechanism: A complex regular expression in the WAF rules triggers catastrophic backtracking or excessive CPU usage when evaluating incoming traffic, leading to CPU exhaustion (HPA at 447%) and failing probes.

hypotheses.statement: The checkout service itself is failing or down, causing edge pods to receive connect and read timeouts.
hypotheses.mechanism: Upstream checkout service unavailability or severe performance degradation forces the edge service to time out on downstream calls.

hypotheses.statement: High traffic load or lack of capacity on edge pods is causing CPU exhaustion and probe failures.
hypotheses.mechanism: Increased traffic or insufficient replica limits prevent edge pods from processing requests in time, causing readiness/liveness probe timeouts.

evidence.rationale: Extremely high CPU utilization (447%) aligns with regex-induced CPU starvation.
Edge pods under heavy CPU starvation are timing out when trying to communicate with dependencies.
Checkout service shows a 5xx error ratio spike and dependency connection errors to inventory, explaining why edge receives timeouts calling it.
Edge pods encounter ConnectTimeout errors calling the checkout dependency, showing external dependency issues are part of the failure mode.

rejected_evidence.reason: quote not found verbatim in the cited observation
quote not found verbatim in the cited observation

alternatives.why_less_likely: Traffic metrics show a drop in request rate rather than a surge, ruling out high traffic volume or simple capacity constraints as the primary cause.
Although upstream checkout dependency issues occurred, metrics and logs correlate the core edge latency and CPU throttling spike precisely with the WAF rule modifications.

uncertainty: The exact regular expression causing the catastrophic backtracking in the edge-waf-rules ConfigMap has not been isolated.
Performance profiling of the regex evaluation engine inside the edge pods would confirm the specific pattern responsible.
remediation: Revert the edge-waf-rules ConfigMap to the previous stable revision.
Review and test all newly added regular expressions for catastrophic backtracking vulnerabilities before deploying them to production.
Implement resource quotas and stricter CPU limits or timeouts on regex evaluations to protect proxy and edge components.

observations.purpose: what is alerting and since when
Check edge pod logs for any WAF-related errors, panic, or long processing times.
Examine CPU and request rate metrics for edge to see the exact onset time relative to the WAF rule change.
Inspect the previous container logs of a restarted edge pod to see if it crashed due to OOM, probe failure, or an unhandled exception related to WAF regex compilation.
Check the health, request rate, error ratio, and CPU/memory metrics of the checkout service to see if checkout is also affected or if it is the root dependency failure.
